phases.title: Define dialog suppression contract
phases.description: Add an engine-level suppression state and a documented --no-dialogs command-line option. Headless mode enables the state automatically, while normal windowed runs retain current modal behavior.

phases.title: Route one-button alerts through the contract
phases.description: Make Windows and shared OS alert paths honor the suppression state without changing crash-handler behavior or multi-choice dialogs.

phases.title: Add bounded headless regression coverage
phases.description: Exercise startup failures and runtime alert paths in hidden, time-bounded child processes so a modal dialog cannot hang the test runner.

phases.title: Document and validate the change
phases.description: Update command-line/API documentation, run the pinned Godot build, and verify the regression harness and repository cleanliness.

tasks.title: Add OS dialog suppression state
tasks.description: Add a default-off OS-level boolean and accessors in core/os/os.h and core/os/os.cpp representing that one-button modal alerts must not block. The suppressed path must preserve the alert title/message through the existing stderr/logger route. Keep this state separate from disable_crash_handler and do not change DisplayServer multi-choice dialog semantics.
acceptance_criteria: The suppression state defaults to disabled for normal runs.
Enabling the state records the same alert text through the existing logging path and returns without waiting for user input.
Crash-handler enablement and suppression state are independent.
The state is available to platform OS alert implementations without introducing a second logging mechanism.
validation: Add or extend the existing OS tests under tests/core/os/test_os.cpp for default state, enablement, and restoration.
Build the Windows editor with pwsh -NoProfile -File .\dev.ps1 build.

tasks.title: Add --no-dialogs and headless defaulting
tasks.description: Update main/main.cpp help text and command-line parsing with --no-dialogs. Parse it early enough that startup and Mono initialization failures can use it. Make --headless set both the existing headless display/audio drivers and the OS dialog suppression state. Preserve --disable-crash-handler as a separate opt-in flag, and do not forward engine flags as project user arguments.
acceptance_criteria: The built executable lists --no-dialogs in --help.
--headless suppresses one-button alerts even when --no-dialogs is omitted.
--no-dialogs independently suppresses one-button alerts when used without --headless.
Existing --headless display/audio behavior and --disable-crash-handler behavior remain unchanged.
validation: Run the pinned console editor with --help and assert that --no-dialogs is present.
Run a bounded startup-failure probe with --headless and without an explicit --no-dialogs flag; assert it exits instead of waiting for a dialog and writes the failure text to its log.

tasks.title: Suppress Windows OS alerts when enabled
tasks.description: Update platform/windows/os_windows.cpp so OS_Windows::alert checks the shared suppression state before calling MessageBoxW. When suppressed, emit the title and message to the existing logger/stderr path and return; when not suppressed, retain the current MessageBoxW behavior. Audit platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp for runtime one-button MessageBoxW calls reachable after command-line parsing and route them through the same policy where feasible. Leave the pre-entry CPU SSE4.2 compatibility dialog out of scope and document why a runtime flag cannot affect it.
acceptance_criteria: A suppressed Windows OS alert never calls a blocking MessageBoxW.
The unsuppressed Windows alert path remains modal and behavior-compatible.
Runtime one-button platform alerts do not bypass the policy after command-line parsing.
The implementation does not disable crash reporting or alter non-OK-only dialogs.
validation: Use a source audit to enumerate remaining MessageBoxW and OS::alert call sites and classify each as covered, unreachable in headless mode, or pre-command-line exception.
Run a Windows process probe for both suppressed and unsuppressed alert policy without allowing an interactive test dialog to remain alive.

tasks.title: Cover startup and Mono alert callers
tasks.description: Audit the existing OS::alert callers in main/main.cpp, modules/mono/mono_gd/gd_mono.cpp, and core/core_bind.cpp. Confirm that missing project data, missing main scene, invalid MainLoop/script startup, missing .NET runtime/assemblies, and script-level OS.alert calls all flow through the shared suppression policy. Add only the minimal caller changes needed if any bypass the policy; preserve the original failure return codes and error messages.
acceptance_criteria: All identified runtime/startup one-button alert callers are non-blocking under headless mode.
Each caller still reports a diagnostic and returns its existing failure status.
No caller silently converts a failure into success.
validation: Use rg to audit OS::get_singleton()->alert and core-bind alert forwarding after the implementation.
Exercise at least one main.cpp failure and one Mono/runtime failure through the integration harness.

tasks.title: Add bounded command-line regression harness
tasks.description: Add a Windows PowerShell integration harness under tests/command_line that resolves the pinned console editor, launches each case with a hidden window, redirects --log-file to a temporary ignored artifact directory, enforces a short timeout, and kills timed-out children. Cover: --headless --help; a missing/invalid project startup failure using --headless without an explicit --no-dialogs flag; the same failure using explicit --no-dialogs; a deterministic script-level OS.alert or runtime alert fixture; and a successful headless invocation proving normal runs still complete. Assert nonzero failure exit codes where expected and require the diagnostic text in the log.
acceptance_criteria: Every expected failure case exits within the timeout instead of waiting for an OK dialog.
Headless mode suppresses dialogs without an explicit extra flag.
Explicit --no-dialogs works independently of --headless.
Failure cases retain nonzero exit codes and diagnostic log content.
The harness leaves no child process running after success, failure, or timeout.
validation: Run the harness once before and once after enabling the implementation in a controlled build to demonstrate the old modal path is detected by timeout and the new path exits normally.
Inspect generated logs for the expected alert text and absence of an interactive dependency.

tasks.title: Document flag and OS.alert behavior
tasks.description: Document --no-dialogs in the command-line help and update doc/classes/OS.xml for alert behavior: normal execution remains modal, while the flag and headless mode route one-button alerts to logs without blocking. Explicitly distinguish this from --disable-crash-handler, multi-choice dialogs, external child-process dialogs, and pre-command-line CPU compatibility dialogs.
acceptance_criteria: Users can discover the flag from --help and the OS.alert API documentation.
Documentation states that suppressed alerts remain diagnostics and do not change failure status.
The documented non-goals match the implemented behavior.
validation: Run the repository XML/documentation validation used by the Godot checkout, if available.
Compare documentation examples with the command-line integration harness cases.

tasks.title: Build and review the complete change
tasks.description: Run the repository doctor and pinned build, execute the command-line regression harness, review the diff for accidental changes to crash handling or normal windowed behavior, and report any remaining pre-entry or external-dialog limitations.
acceptance_criteria: The pinned Windows editor build succeeds.
The bounded headless regression harness passes.
The final diff is limited to the dialog policy, its tests, and documentation.
Remaining unsupported dialog sources are explicitly listed.
validation: Run git diff --check and inspect git status in repos/godot.
